note: Every lifecycle the scan can find, with who owns it and how it is handled. `classification` is one of: migrated (in src/shared/stateMachines.json), not-migrated (a real machine with states and events that is not in the registry yet) or not-a-machine (a status label, boolean, linear progress value or one-shot classification with no transitions to guard). `scan` lists the lifecycle-scan keys this entry covers; every key scripts/lib/lifecycle-scan.mjs returns must appear exactly once.

lifecycles.title: Model server
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `server`. The generated Rust enum is the host's source of truth and the renderer reads the same names.

lifecycles.title: Voice chat and the voice worker
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `voice` for the conversation; the worker's own off/starting/ready/failed is covered by the same entry.

lifecycles.title: File build, its steps and its stages
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `build` for the overall result; the step and stage statuses are its supporting labels.

lifecycles.title: Model benchmark run
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `bench`. The runner's every phase change in `set` goes through `canTransition('bench', …)`; the transitions were taken from the real paths, including the provider-retry loading → installing move.

lifecycles.title: First-launch setup steps
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `setup`. Each step's state change goes through `canTransition('setup', …)` in SetupService.set, so an impossible move is reported.

lifecycles.title: Harness run
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `run`. Every createRun moves through nextState('run', ...) per step and at the outcome; an illegal move is logged, never a crash mid-run. A journal step's status is a record label of the same machine, and the run view sent to the screen (phase 11) carries the same labels, read-only.

lifecycles.title: Knowledge index of one project
lifecycles.where: src/shared/stateMachines.json; src/core/knowledge/store.ts (the build drives the events); src/renderer/Projects.tsx (the observed state)
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `knowledgeIndex`. The store's build goes through the machine's events; the Project knowledge screen shows the state observed from the store.

lifecycles.title: Computer Use agent run
lifecycles.where: src/shared/stateMachines.json; src/sidecar/computerUse.ts (the loop settles it, settle is the only writer of the final status); src/renderer/AgentPanel.tsx (the observed state)
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `agentRun` for the run's verdict (running, done, unresolved, failed, cancelled). The step phases (observe, propose, act, verify, settled) are supporting labels the events carry, read-only — the person's stop settles cancelled, never failed.

lifecycles.title: Observation feed freshness
lifecycles.reason: A pure function of a reading's timestamp, failure count and the clock, recomputed on every render. Nothing stores a phase and nothing fires events, so there is no move to guard.

lifecycles.title: Sidecar settings save
lifecycles.reason: A label read from two fields (a call in flight, a patch waiting); nothing stores it and nothing moves it by event. The host's settings write is the one writer and its lock is the guard.

lifecycles.title: Model preload
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `preload`. The controller's phase change goes through `canTransition('preload', …)` (a null phase is the machine's idle state), so an impossible move is reported.

lifecycles.title: Application update check
lifecycles.reason: Structurally a status chain (checking → current/downloading/ready/error) but the updater is disabled: every method forces the error state and there is no transport. It has no transitions to guard until a real update feed exists.

lifecycles.title: Model download and install progress
lifecycles.reason: A linear progress flow (checking → downloading → done/error/cancelled) where the only changing value is a percentage, not a set of states with events.

lifecycles.title: Voice model download progress
lifecycles.reason: A linear download progress flow (downloading → extracting → done/error/cancelled); no transitions to guard.

lifecycles.title: NPU load test
lifecycles.reason: A running boolean plus an append-only attempt log; no phases and no transitions.

lifecycles.title: Sub-agent run
lifecycles.reason: A linear run card status (running → done/error). The card only shows the end.

lifecycles.title: Code review run
lifecycles.reason: A linear run card status (running → done).

lifecycles.title: Improve loop run
lifecycles.reason: A linear run card status (running → done).

lifecycles.title: Scheduled task result
lifecycles.where: src/shared/types.ts (`TaskRun.status`); src/core/scheduler.ts; src/sidecar/register/tasks.ts (`runTask` records a busy refusal as an error result)
lifecycles.reason: A terminal result (ok/error) plus a running boolean; the scheduler has no state to transition.

lifecycles.title: Work log line state
lifecycles.reason: A per-line UI label (done/running/waiting/error) derived from the build and agent pipelines; it has no events of its own.

lifecycles.title: Evidence freshness for a model artifact
lifecycles.reason: A classification of evidence validity (present/stale/absent), computed from timestamps, not a lifecycle.

lifecycles.title: Memory estimate phase
lifecycles.reason: UI feedback for one estimate request (idle/busy/ready and so on); no transitions to guard.

lifecycles.title: Provider connection test
lifecycles.reason: A button feedback state (idle/busy/ok/failed); no lifecycle.

lifecycles.title: Step icon state
lifecycles.reason: Presentation state for one icon (running/done/waiting/error), fed by the build statuses.

lifecycles.title: Construct scenario step
lifecycles.reason: The kind of one test-scenario action (click, key, wait); a value union, not a state flow.

lifecycles.title: Template kit language phase and status
lifecycles.reason: Per-language progress labels inside a template build step; no transitions.

lifecycles.title: Renderer local status aliases
lifecycles.reason: Local type aliases that only rename a host state shape (`Awaited<ReturnType<...>>`); they add no lifecycle.

lifecycles.title: NPU owner
lifecycles.where: src/shared/stateMachines.json; src/core/npuOwner.ts (NpuOwner.claim is the one way an engine takes the NPU); src/sidecar/main.ts (both engines' starts and the window's releaseFoundry)
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `npuOwner` (free, geniex, foundry; a jump from one engine to the other is forbidden). It was implicit, spread over two unconditional releases added after two crashes; tests/one-engine-guard.test.ts fails on a start that does not claim.

lifecycles.title: Model verdict on this PC
lifecycles.where: src/shared/stateMachines.json; src/core/loadFailures.ts (verdictOf, checkOutcome); src/sidecar/main.ts (the unknown-model check ends with the machine's event); src/core/modelList.ts (listedHere)
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `modelVerdict` (unknown, checking, loads, fails), read from the placements and loadFailures records. It was implicit in two records written in separate places; a check GenieX never tried is now the event not_tried and records nothing.

lifecycles.title: Computer Use window grant
lifecycles.where: src/shared/stateMachines.json; src-tauri/src/agent_driver.rs (the grant slot); src/renderer/computerUse.tsx (releases a grant whose run failed to start)
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `agentGrant` (free, held) for the docs and the legal moves; the host's grant slot is still an Option, and a generated Rust enum is owed once the host builds again.

lifecycles.title: GenieX options probe
lifecycles.where: src/shared/stateMachines.json; src-tauri/src/capabilities.rs (help_is_complete decides complete or partial; only a complete answer is kept)
lifecycles.reason: Registered machine `geniexProbe` (not_probed, complete, partial) for the docs and the legal moves; the host keeps only a complete answer. A generated Rust enum is owed once the host builds again.

lifecycles.title: Model switch in Settings (Starting, Warming up, Cancel)
lifecycles.reason: One switch's view: idle, starting, warming, then done (idle), failed or cancelled. It mirrors the registered `server` machine (starting, loading, ready) read from the host and adds only the person's Cancel; registering it would duplicate the server's transitions.

lifecycles.title: GenieX minimum-version verdict
lifecycles.reason: A one-shot classification of the installed geniex.exe and its `--version` output (ok, missing, outdated, invalid), recomputed whenever the executable's identity changes. It is a verdict, not a stored phase: nothing moves from one value to another by an event.
